comparison: Perfect agreement on DMH1 treatment data (C9, C64-C72, C74). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing that Bmp signaling inhibition leads to supernumerary ampullary organs and ectopic neuromasts, supporting an inhibitory role for Bmp signaling.

Strong agreement on Bmp5 crispant data (C8, C54-C63, C73, C87-C89). Both evaluations accept the CRISPR/Cas9 knockout evidence as convincing that Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ formation. Peer review describes this as part of 'convincing evidence' using 'targeted gene knock-out'.

Disagreement on interpretation of opposing Bmp roles (C10-C12). OpenEval finds the synthesis of CRISPR and DMH1 data logically sound and well-demonstrated. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, stating 'It remains unclear if the opposing effects of Bmp can be adequately accounted for' and request additional experiments to test temporal effects.
Agreement on prior RNA-seq screen data (C5, C25-C27). Both evaluations accept the foundational differential expression data from Modrell et al. 2017a as appropriate rationale for investigating Bmp5.
Agreement on Bmp5 expression pattern data (C6, C28-C32). Both evaluations accept the in situ hybridization observations across developmental stages as descriptive findings foundational to the study.

Agreement on pSMAD1/5/9 immunohistochemistry data (C7, C33-C40). Both evaluations accept the systematic protein localization data across developmental stages, though OpenEval notes some speculation about nerve localization.
Agreement on Bmp4 expression data (C41-C46). Both evaluations accept the in situ hybridization findings, though OpenEval notes the inference about an unidentified ligand (C46) remains speculative.

Agreement on Bmp antagonist expression data (C47-C53). Both evaluations accept the expression patterns of Bambi, Chrd, and Grem2, with OpenEval noting appropriate caution about functional role inferences.
Agreement on technical aspects of CRISPR design (C54-C56, C87-C88). Both evaluations accept the genome analysis and sgRNA specificity claims as part of the convincing knockout evidence.

OpenEval evaluated background/contextual claims from literature (C1-C3, C13-C24) as appropriately cited established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated literature claims about Bmp in inner ear development (C75-C80) as appropriately cited established knowledge used for contextualization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval found claims about ampullary organs as 'default' fate (C81-C83) to be speculative and requiring additional validation beyond cited Foxg1 work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval found claims about nerve-mediated Bmp signaling (C84-C86) to be explicitly speculative, lacking direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval found claims about Bmp5's role in regeneration (C90-C94) to be speculative, as no regeneration experiments were performed in sterlet to test this hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluated claims about electroreception evolution and model system rationale (C4, C25) as well-established facts appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
